trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Read in full: two short noun-phrase-headed sections (even-odd selection; regime transitions) with one display. Judged all ten categories; the prose is plain and carries no rhetorical construction.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: TWO NUMERIC DEFECTS reported, not fixed. (1) 'of the 254 stable nuclides, 166 have even p and even n' -- 166 matches no published tally; the standard figure is 148 (of 251) or 150 (of 253-254) even-even nuclides, i.e. about 59 percent, whereas 166/254 = 65.4 percent. Needs a cited source or correction. (2) The stated beta-decay threshold A_k = (a_C(2k+1)/(2a_A))^(3/2) does not follow from the parent proposition's own p*(A) = a_A A / (2(a_A + a_C A^(2/3))). Solved p*(A) = k + 1/2 numerically at standard liquid-drop coefficients (a_C = 0.71 MeV, a_A = 4 a_sym = 92.8 MeV, the normalisation the parent's E(p,A) implies): exact A_20 = 44.97, A_50 = 119.78, A_91 = 236.55 -- the last correctly landing on uranium, and the model itself checks out (p*(238) = 91.98 vs Z = 92; p*(208) = 81.98 vs Z = 82). The stated formula gives 0.062, 0.240, 0.586 for the same k. Coefficient-free argument that the SHAPE is wrong: a_C > 0 forces p*(A) < A/2, so p* = k + 1/2 requires A_k > 2k+1 for every k, while (a_C(2k+1)/(2a_A))^(3/2) falls below 2k+1 for any a_C/(2a_A) < (2k+1)^(-1/3). RETRACTION of my own first pass: I initially proposed exponent 3 (the large-A limit A_k = ((2k+1)a_C/a_A)^3); that also fails numerically (0.031, 0.46, 2.74), because a_A and a_C A^(2/3) are comparable across the whole physical range (93 vs 27 at A = 238), so NEITHER asymptotic limit is available and no closed form of this shape is correct. The remaining sentences check out: at p* = k + 1/2 the parabola is symmetric about the half-integer, so (k, A-k) and (k+1, A-k-1) do have equal binding.
